title: Agents get spending limits while banks plan for fewer desks
dek: Barclays tied a 5,000-job plan to AI, Walmart gave shoppers spending caps for agents, and a report says hackers pointed agents at banks.

body.head: AI shows up in headcount plans
body.text: Barclays has revealed plans to cut 5,000 jobs, about 5% of its workforce, as part of an AI-linked efficiency push, according to CNBC. About 60% of the cuts are expected in support functions, including developers, and the bank's earnings presentation described "organisational simplification and technology change efficiency driven by AI."
support: British lender Barclays has revealed plans to cut 5,000 jobs — about 5% of its total workforce — as part of an artificial intelligence-linked efficiency push.

About 60% of the cuts are expected to be in support functions, including developers, according to the earnings presentation, which also noted an outcome was "organisational simplification and technology change efficiency driven by AI."

body.head: Walmart caps what agents can spend
body.text: Meanwhile Walmart launched its Agent Gateway, which lets an AI agent search its online inventory and make purchases on behalf of the agent's user. Customers will be able to approve each transaction or authorize transactions within a spending limit they set, and Walmart says agents can't access the customers' payment information.
support: It starts with Walmart’s Agent Gateway, the company’s new MCP server, which is designed to help approved agents connect to Walmart over the model context protocol (MCP).
In this case, it lets an AI agent search across Walmart’s online inventory and make purchases on behalf of the agent’s user.
Plus, customers will be in control of how purchases get approved by either requiring approval for each transaction or by authorizing transactions within a certain spending limit they set.
Walmart also says that agents can’t take actions beyond what the shopper intends, can’t access the customers’ payment information, and can only access the information they need for the given task.

body.head: Agents on the attacking side
body.text: At the same time, a report on Wednesday from The Information said the hackers used a web of AI agents powered by models such as Anthropic's Claude and SpaceX's Grok to attack more than 400 targets in Latin America, including banks and payments companies. The report also included a statement from Anthropic saying it began an investigation and quickly blocked the hackers' use of Claude.
support: That’s according to a report Wednesday (Oct. 21) from The Information, citing research by the cybersecurity startup Straiker shared exclusively with the news outlet.

According to the report, the hackers used a web of AI agents powered by models such as Anthropic’s Claude and SpaceX’s Grok to attack more than 400 targets in Latin America, including banks and payments companies.
The report also included a statement from Anthropic which said it began an investigation after Straiker revealed its findings, and quickly blocked the hackers’ use of Claude.

body.head: A question for our own desks
body.text: For those of us who plan teams and approve agent projects in a bank or lender, the useful questions sit side by side: which support work is being redesigned, who sets the spending limit for each agent, and who reviews what an agent is allowed to touch?
